subject: ventures/h1b-weighted-lottery-odds-calculator
professional: an immigration attorney or HR-immigration specialist who advises employers on H-1B cap registration, plus a statistician for the draw model

evidence.correctness: Ran `node -e` against calc.mjs and an independent Python script (Newton solver for lambda, separate code path, plus Efraimidis-Spirakis exact successive weighted draws, 300 trials, pool scaled 1/100). DEFAULT_POOL, 100000 first-draw selections, weights 4/3/2/1 per the DHS weighted selection final rule: independent lambda 0.171622 vs calc 0.171622; regular odds L1..L4 0.15770/0.29054/0.40242/0.49666 identical to calc to 1e-15; advanced-degree odds 0.29333/0.50061/0.64710/0.75061 identical; evaluate(sampleList) Asha 0.5006, Chen 0.7506 match. Exact-draw Monte Carlo (0.1569/0.2913/0.4040/0.4955) and a 75-registration stress pool (exact 0.336/0.561/0.709/0.807 vs approx 0.337/0.560/0.708/0.807) confirm the exp approximation is accurate, so the page's 'close for pools this large' is backed. Departure: the master's-cap order is regular draw first, then advanced-degree draw among leftovers (calc.mjs:30-34, page 'Advanced-degree draw'). To my knowledge, the current process (since the 2019 reversal) selects the advanced-degree cap first and then the regular cap from all remaining registrations; I could not fetch the rule text through the proxy to confirm, so this is flagged unverified. If right, advanced odds are mis-stated. Also parseCsv wrong-input cases: 'Senior' parses silently as level 1, and 'Level II' / 'Level IV' give NaN and an error row. Capped at 2 for the unconfirmed order and the silent misparse.
evidence.completeness: Checked each claimed feature by running it: CSV/TSV paste parsing with 1-4 or I-IV (works for bare numerals; 'Level IV' style fails), per-candidate weighted odds vs flat (works), one-level-higher gain (works, null at level IV), at-least-one probability (works, 0.9557 for sample), advanced-degree second draw (works, subject to the order caveat), per-line error rows (works), CSV report download (reportCsv runs; 6 lines for 5 candidates), usage counting and opt-out (usage.mjs, 22 tests pass), llms.txt, robots, sitemap present. No stubs or TODOs found. Related-tool links resolve (page.test.mjs). Page JS was read, not run in a browser.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the venture dir: 22 tests, 22 pass, 0 fail. Mutations (reverted by git checkout, tree clean afterward): (1) WEIGHTS level IV 4 -> 5: caught, 1 test failed (the weights deepEqual). (2) advanced = regular + second, dropping the (1 - regular) factor: caught, 2 tests failed. (3) advanced-draw pool ignoring first-draw selection (unsel = counts * advancedShare, dropping the (1 - pOf(lam1,l)) factor): NOT caught, 22 of 22 pass. So the second-stage pool logic is unprotected. No test compares any number to an independent value (all tests are monotonicity, sums, or self-consistency), and nothing tests the parser on quoted fields, 'Level IV' or free text.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (91 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script. The engine is compact, pure and readable; bisection solver is correct and handles target >= total (Infinity) and zero. Defects: parseCsv's level cleaning strips everything except 0-9ivIV, so any text containing an i (e.g. 'Senior') becomes Level I silently, and 'Level IV' loses its Roman numeral to the stray 'v' and fails; no quoted-CSV support (split on delimiter); advanced flag is false for any value other than y/yes/true/1, so 'Maybe' or blank silently counts as no; Math.round of pool counts and NaN to 0 silent; evaluate returns level NaN rows. Inputs like negative or non-numeric pool values fall back to 0 without telling the user. Maximum tooling hygiene otherwise: no network calls, escapes HTML output.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'nothing uploaded' (page.test.mjs asserts no fetch/XHR/beacon; I grepped index.html and calc.mjs, none found; backed). Weights 1-4 (calc.mjs WEIGHTS and my recompute; backed against the rule). 'Close for pools this large' (backed by my Monte Carlo). Disclaimer, no-warranty, not-affiliated, data-handling, sponsor and MIT link present in the footer (page.test.mjs). Default pool labelled illustrative (page and VENTURE.yaml; backed). Not backed: 'Rules reviewed 2026-10-06 from the published final rule' gives no Federal Register or USCIS citation anywhere on the page or README, so a reader cannot check it. llms.txt links to the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address instead of https://marisstella.app/h1b-weighted-lottery-odds-calculator/. README test command uses a glob from the repo root that Node 22 does not expand the way the other ventures document. Footer 'Not affiliated with any court, housing agency' is boilerplate that does not fit (court and housing agency). Page says the model does not decide filing rate, which is honest.
evidence.fitness: Walked an HR lead's job: paste five candidates, set a pool guess, read per-person odds and the value of a raise to the next level. It works in one click on the sample and yields a useful report. Gaps a practitioner hits in the first hour: the pool inputs are guesses with no real FY2026/FY2027 registration counts or selection numbers to start from (the weighted rule's first real data may exist; none is cited), 'Selected in the first draw' defaults to 100000 without explaining how USCIS's 65,000 + 20,000 caps and over-selection for filing rates map to it, no per-candidate multiple-registration handling, and Level labels like 'Level IV' in a pasted spreadsheet fail. Useful as a planning aid, not yet something an attorney would hand to a client.
evidence.domain: Compared against the DHS weighted selection final rule (entries 4/3/2/1 for wage levels IV..I, selection by wage level the offered salary meets, one registration per beneficiary, advanced-degree cap) and standard successive-draw probability. Weights and the lambda approximation are right. Departures: (a) master's cap order, see correctness; (b) it treats the first-draw count as a free parameter, leaving the reader to work out 65,000 + 20,000 plus the over-selection USCIS does; (c) no handling of the rule's wage-level assignment when a job has multiple SOC codes or areas of intended employment (stated as not decided, to its credit); (d) no mention of the lowest-level rule for wages that fall between levels. A senior immigration practitioner would use it for rough intuition and verify against USCIS numbers.

defects.what: Advanced-degree stage is modelled after the regular draw (leftover advanced registrations get a second chance); the current process selects the advanced-degree cap first and then the regular cap from all remaining registrations. Not confirmed against rule text (proxy blocked); verify before changing, then update calc.mjs, the page text and tests.

parseCsv silently turns any text containing the letter i (e.g. 'Senior') into wage level 1, and 'Level IV' / 'Level II' cell values fail (stray v and e/l stripped to 'v'); a wrong level changes the odds shown with no warning.
Second-stage pool logic is untested: removing the (1 - first-draw selection probability) factor in the advanced-degree pool still passes all 22 tests; no test compares to an independent number.
No citation (Federal Register or USCIS URL) for the rule the weights were read from.
llms.txt links to the retired GitHub Pages address, not marisstella.app.

Boilerplate 'Not affiliated with any court, housing agency' does not fit an H-1B tool; no CSV quoted-field support; advanced flag silently false for unrecognised values; the 'node --test ventures/.../**/*.test.mjs' README command is not the documented form.

verdict: A small, honest, working planning tool whose core math is right: independent recomputation of the lambda solve, all eight per-level odds and the sample report matched to 1e-15, and an exact weighted-draw Monte Carlo agrees with the approximation to about 0.2 points, so the page's accuracy claim is backed. It does not yet meet the senior-professional bar: the advanced-degree draw order appears to differ from the current process (unconfirmed), the CSV level parser silently misreads free text and 'Level IV', and the tests are self-consistency checks that missed one of three seeded mutations (second-stage pool). The page also cites no source for the rule and llms.txt points at a retired URL. Finished (every claimed feature works) but not at the bar; correctness, claims and verification all score 2. Unrecorded: browser run of the page script.
